paras: The killing of Ben Burnett was the fatal shooting of a Black man by the city marshal of Lamonte, Missouri, ten miles west of Sedalia, on the evening of March 1, 1881. The marshal, named in the fullest account as Philip Zilhart, said Burnett had refused arrest after attacking a woman and advanced on him with a club, and a coroner's jury found the shooting justified. Wire reports carried the story to Memphis and Chicago, and a longer Sedalia dispatch ran in the Dallas Herald under the headline "A Brutal Negro Done For."

According to a Sedalia dispatch of March 4, Burnett lived with a "mistress," having driven off his "lawful wife" the previous spring. That dispatch said he came home drunk with a jug of hard cider on the evening of the shooting, and that when the woman poured it out he flew into a rage and got a gun. She fled to the house of a white neighbor named Chaffey, where, by the same account, Burnett followed her and struck her on the head with a stone crock before going home.

The woman went looking for an officer and, on returning, was driven back to Chaffey's house by Burnett, who had taken up a large club and threatened to kill her. Chaffey, at home this time, warned him off, and the March 4 dispatch says Burnett struck at him several times; the earlier wire said only that Chaffey forbade him to enter his yard or house.

At that point the marshal arrived and ordered Burnett to surrender. In the marshal's account as the papers gave it, Burnett cursed him, refused to be taken and advanced with his club, and kept coming after a second order to stop. The marshal fired, then snapped his pistol at him several more times; Burnett sank to the ground and died within a few minutes.

Coroner King examined the case, and his jury returned the verdict "Killed in self-defense." The wire reported simply that a coroner's jury "justified the act of the Marshal," while a Chillicothe paper rendered the verdict as "justifiable murder." No report of an arrest, charge or trial of the marshal appears in the coverage.

The first reports came from a Sedalia wire dated March 2, which the Memphis Daily Appeal printed as "Shot by an Officer" and the Chicago Daily Tribune as "Killed by an Officer" on March 3. The Tribune also listed the item in its "Criminal News" column deck as "A Negro Who Resisted Arrest Shot Dead by an Officer of the Law." The wire spelled the marshal's name "Telhart" or "Zelhart" and told the story entirely from his side, calling Burnett "the negro" who advanced "in a menacing manner."

A longer dispatch from Sedalia, dated March 4, ran in the Dallas Daily Herald on March 5 and again in the Dallas Weekly Herald on March 10 under the headline "A Brutal Negro Done For." It added the cider, the gun and the stone crock, called Burnett "the enraged negro," and gave the marshal's name as Philip Zilhart. In Missouri the Weekly Chillicothe Crisis gave the killing one sentence on March 10. No paper printed an account from the woman or from any Black resident of Lamonte.

The accounts differ in detail rather than substance: the wire has Burnett chasing the woman to Chaffey's with a club, while the March 4 dispatch describes an earlier attack with a stone crock and blows aimed at Chaffey. Both versions come from the Sedalia side and agree that the marshal shot Burnett as he advanced and that the inquest cleared the marshal.

reader.title: Killing of Ben Burnett
bases: A town marshal acting alone shot a Black man he was trying to arrest; no crowd or posse took part (A1, A3, A6).

Two separate Sedalia dispatches, the March 2 wire (A1, A3) and the March 4 report (A4, A6), plus a Missouri brief (A5) agree that the Lamonte city marshal shot Burnett dead and that a coroner's jury cleared him, though all rest on the marshal's side of events.

accounts.label: Sedalia wire, March 2
accounts.gist: Drunk, Burnett beat his mistress and chased her with a club to a neighbor's; when the marshal ordered him to surrender he advanced 'in a menacing manner' and was shot; the coroner's jury justified the marshal.

accounts.label: Sedalia dispatch, March 4 (Dallas Herald)
accounts.gist: A longer version: Burnett raged after the woman poured out his cider, got a gun, struck her with a stone crock in Chaffey's house, returned with a club and struck at Chaffey; he cursed the marshal and advanced, and kept coming after the first shot; Coroner King's jury found 'Killed in self-defense.'

accounts.label: Missouri brief
accounts.gist: Burnett was killed at Lamonte by the city marshal and the coroner's jury returned a verdict of 'justifiable murder'.

framing.detail: The Memphis Appeal and Chicago Tribune ran the March 2 wire under 'Shot by an Officer' and 'Killed by an Officer', telling it from the marshal's side and calling Burnett 'the negro'.
The Chicago Tribune's column deck read 'A Negro Who Resisted Arrest Shot Dead by an Officer of the Law'.
The Dallas Herald headed the fuller dispatch 'A Brutal Negro Done For' and called Burnett 'the enraged negro'.
The Chillicothe Crisis gave a one-line notice of the killing and verdict.
